facts.statement: The genus Bugenasaura was once considered a synonym of Thescelosaurus but is now rejected.
facts.quote: synonyms: Bugenasaura Galton, 1995

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus edmontonensis is a species described by Sternberg in 1940 that is currently considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: T. edmontonensis Sternberg, 1940 (nomen dubium)

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus infernalis was named by Galton in 1995 but is now regarded as a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: T. infernalis (Galton, 1995) (nomen dubium)

facts.statement: Thescelosaurids are debated as being either basal ornithopods or placed outside the ornithopod group within Neornithischia.
facts.quote: Thescelosaurids are either considered to be basal ("primitive") ornithopods, or are placed outside of this group within the broader group Neornithischia.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the late Maastrichtian age.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous (late Maastrichtian),

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus lived around 66 million years ago, making it one of the last non-avian dinosaurs before the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.
facts.quote: Living during the late Maastrichtian age, it was among the last of the non-avian dinosaurs before the entire group went extinct during the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event around 66 million years ago.

facts.statement: Adult Thescelosaurus measured roughly 3 to 4 meters in length and weighed between 200 and 300 kilograms.
facts.quote: Adult Thescelosaurus would have measured roughly 3-4 m long and probably weighed 200 to 300 kg.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus was a bipedal dinosaur with a tail that made up half its body length and was stiffened by ossified tendons.
facts.quote: It moved on two legs, and its body was counter-balanced by its long tail, which made up half of the body length and was stiffened by rod-like ossified tendons.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had a long, low snout that terminated in a toothless beak.
facts.quote: The animal had a long, low snout that ended in a toothless beak.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus possessed five fingers on its hands and four toes on its feet.
facts.quote: The hand bore five fingers, and the foot four toes.

facts.statement: Thin plates were found along the sides of Thescelosaurus ribs, though their function remains unclear.
facts.quote: Thin plates are found next to the ribs' sides, the function of which is unclear.

facts.statement: Scale impressions have been preserved on the leg of one Thescelosaurus specimen.
facts.quote: Scale impressions are known from the leg of one specimen.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus was an herbivore that likely fed selectively based on its specialized teeth and narrow snout.
facts.quote: An herbivore, Thescelosaurus was likely a selective feeder, as indicated by its teeth and narrow snout.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had robust limbs with a femur longer than its tibia, suggesting it was not adapted for running.
facts.quote: Its limbs were robust, and its femur (thigh bone) was longer than its tibia (shin bone), suggesting that it was not adapted to running.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had a comparatively small brain, which may indicate it lived in small groups of two to three individuals.
facts.quote: Its brain was comparatively small, possibly indicating small group sizes of two to three individuals.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Thescelosaurus might have been a burrowing animal, based on its acute sense of smell and poor hearing.
facts.quote: It might have been burrowing, as acute smell and poor hearing are typical for modern burrowing animals.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus is the namesake genus of the family Thescelosauridae.
facts.quote: Thescelosaurus is the eponymous member of its family, the Thescelosauridae.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus fossils have been found in western North America, including the Lance Formation in Wyoming and formations in North Dakota, South Dakota, Montana, Alberta, and Saskatchewan.
facts.quote: The first specimens were discovered in the Lance Formation of Wyoming, but subsequent discoveries have been made in North Dakota, South Dakota, Montana, Alberta, and Saskatchewan, in geological formations including the Frenchman Formation, Hell Creek Formation, and Scollard Formation.

facts.statement: A near-complete skeleton of Thescelosaurus was discovered in July 1891 by John Bell Hatcher and William H. Utterback along Doegie Creek in Wyoming.
facts.quote: In July 1891, the fossil hunter John Bell Hatcher, who had been hired by Marsh, and his assistant William H. Utterback discovered a near-complete skeleton of a small herbivorous dinosaur along Doegie Creek in Niobrara County, Wyoming, in rocks of the Lance Formation.

facts.statement: Charles W. Gilmore discovered the neglected skeleton of a new dinosaur species in 1913.
facts.quote: It was not before 1913 that Gilmore opened the box and, to his surprise, found the skeleton of a new species of dinosaur.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus neglectus was formally named and described by Charles W. Gilmore in 1913.
facts.quote: In 1913, Gilmore published a preliminary description naming the new genus and species Thescelosaurus neglectus.

facts.statement: The name Thescelosaurus is derived from the Greek words for 'marvelous' and 'reptile' or 'lizard'.
facts.quote: The generic name derives from the Greek words θέσκελος (), marvelous, and σαυρος () reptile or lizard.

facts.statement: The specific name 'neglectus' means 'neglected' or 'overlooked' because the type specimen was ignored for many years.
facts.quote: The specific name, neglectus, is Latin for neglected or overlooked, as the type specimen had been unattended to for so long.

facts.statement: A Thescelosaurus specimen unearthed in 1999 was once thought to contain a fossilized heart, but this identification is now doubted by scientists.
facts.quote: The genus attracted media attention in 2000, when a specimen unearthed in 1999 was interpreted as including a fossilized heart, but scientists now doubt the identification of the object.

facts.statement: While burrowing is confirmed in the related Oryctodromeus, it might have been a widespread behavior among thescelosaurids.
facts.quote: Burrowing has been confirmed for the closely related Oryctodromeus, and might have been widespread in thescelosaurids.

facts.statement: William Parks described the species T. warreni in 1926 based on a skeleton found in the Edmonton Formation of Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: In 1926, William Parks described the new species T. warreni from a well-preserved skeleton from Alberta, Canada, from what was then known as the Edmonton Formation.

facts.statement: Charles M. Sternberg named the species T. edmontonensis in 1940 based on specimen CMN 8537 found in the Edmonton Formation of Rumsey, Alberta.
facts.quote: In 1940, Sternberg named an additional species, T. edmontonensis, based on another articulated skeleton (CMN 8537) that he had discovered in the Edmonton Formation of Rumsey, Alberta.

facts.statement: Four specimens of Thescelosaurus were collected by Barnum Brown in Montana in 1906 and 1909 from the Hell Creek Formation.
facts.quote: These include four specimens from the Hell Creek Formation collected by Barnum Brown in Montana in 1906 and 1909

facts.statement: Levi Sternberg discovered two specimens of Thescelosaurus in 1921 in the Frenchman Formation of Rocky Creek, Saskatchewan.
facts.quote: two specimens found in 1921 by Levi Sternberg in the Frenchman Formation of Rocky Creek, Saskatchewan

facts.statement: William J. Morris described two partial skeletons found in 1976 in the Hell Creek Formation of Garfield County, Montana, by preparator Harli Garbani.
facts.quote: William J. Morris described three additional partial skeletons in 1976, two found in the Hell Creek Formation of Garfield County, Montana by preparator Harli Garbani

facts.statement: In 1995, Peter M. Galton revised Thescelosaurus, arguing that the ankle traits of T. edmontonensis were due to breakage and actually matched T. neglectus.
facts.quote: Galton revised Thescelosaurus for a second time in 1995. He argued that the supposedly diagnostic traits of the ankle of the T. edmontonensis specimen are the result of breakage, as indicated by the previously undescribed left ankle of that specimen that showed the same anatomy as T. neglectus.

facts.statement: A tooth assigned to Bugenasaura was reported to come from the Late Jurassic Kimmeridge Clay Formation of England, making it roughly 70 million years older than the type specimen.
facts.quote: Significantly, this tooth reportedly came from the Late Jurassic-era Kimmeridge Clay Formation of Weymouth, England, and therefore is roughly 70 million years older than the Bugenasaura type specimen and from another continent.

facts.statement: The specimen nicknamed "Willo" (NCSM 15728) was found in 1999 in the upper Hell Creek Formation of Harding County, South Dakota, by Michael Hammer.
facts.quote: The key specimen, however, was NCSM 15728, nicknamed "Willo", which was found in the upper Hell Creek Formation in Harding County, South Dakota by Michael Hammer in 1999.

facts.statement: The "Willo" specimen preserves a complete skull that revealed the animal had a lower and longer skull than previously thought.
facts.quote: "Willo" also includes a complete skull, showing that it was much lower and longer than previously thought.

facts.statement: New specimens including "Willo" led researchers to assign Bugenasaura infernalis back to the genus Thescelosaurus.
facts.quote: "Willo" and the other new specimens made it clear that Bugenasaura infernalis must be assigned to Thescelosaurus.

facts.statement: Caleb M. Brown and colleagues named the species T. assiniboiensis in 2011 based on specimen RSM P 1225.1 found in 1968 by Albert Swanston.
facts.quote: Another species, T. assiniboiensis, was named by Caleb M. Brown and colleagues in 2011 based on a specimen (RSM P 1225.1) found in 1968 by Albert Swanston, a museum technician at the Royal Saskatchewan Museum.

facts.statement: A specimen of Thescelosaurus was reported found at the Tanis fossil site in North Dakota in 2022, which shows signs of the Chicxulub asteroid impact.
facts.quote: In 2022, news media reported that a specimen of Thescelosaurus was found at the Tanis fossil site in North Dakota, which is thought to show direct signs of the Chicxulub asteroid impact in the Gulf of Mexico that resulted in the K-Pg extinction.

facts.statement: The name Bugenasaura combines the Latin words for large cheek and the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The name is a combination of the Latin bu, large and gena, cheek, as well as the Ancient Greek saura, lizard.

facts.statement: Specimen AMNH 5034 was found just 5 feet below the Fort Union Formation, representing the youngest locality where dinosaurs have been found.
facts.quote: One of Browns specimens, AMNH 5034, was found just 5 ft below the Fort Union Formation, at the youngest locality from which dinosaurs were found.

facts.statement: William J. Morris suggested that T. edmontonensis and T. garbanii might be separated from Thescelosaurus as a new genus, arguing their ankle anatomy was distinct from T. neglectus.
facts.quote: Morris also argued that the ankle of T. edmontonensis, which Galton claimed was damaged and misinterpreted, was truly different from T. neglectus and more similar to T. garbanii. Therefore, he suggested that T. edmontonensis and T. garbanii may eventually be separated from Thescelosaurus as a new genus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the hindlimb of T. garbanii actually belongs to the pachycephalosaurid Stygimoloch instead.
facts.quote: There was also the possibility that the hindlimb of T. garbanii did instead belong to the pachycephalosaurid Stygimoloch, which is also known from the Hell Creek Formation and for which the hindlimb was unknown.

facts.statement: It is debated whether a tooth assigned to Bugenasaura was mislabelled and actually from the Lance Formation of Wyoming rather than the Kimmeridge Clay Formation of England.
facts.quote: Galton argued that it had possibly been mislabelled and was actually from the Lance Formation of Wyoming, but the tooth was first collected before the museum was active in the Lance region.

facts.statement: Due to a lack of diagnostic features, some researchers classified a tooth previously assigned to Bugenasaura as an indeterminate ornithischian in 2011.
facts.quote: The lack of diagnostic features led Paul M. Barrett and Susannah Maidment to classify the tooth as an indeterminate ornithischian in 2011.

facts.statement: Boyd and colleagues considered the new combination T. infernalis undiagnostic after reassigning Bugenasaura infernalis to Thescelosaurus.
facts.quote: By reassigning the species, Boyd and colleagues created the new combination T. infernalis which they considered undiagnostic.

facts.statement: The assignment of most Thescelosaurus specimens to specific species remained uncertain because overlapping bone material for direct comparison was often unavailable.
facts.quote: Specimens can only be directly compared if they preserve the same bones, but overlapping material is often not available – the assignment of most Thescelosaurus specimens to any of the three recognized species therefore remained uncertain.

facts.statement: The largest known Thescelosaurus species, T. garbanii, was estimated to be 4 to 4.5 meters long and weigh between 200 and 300 kilograms.
facts.quote: The largest known thescelosaurid, its body length has been estimated at 2.5 – 4.0 m and the weight at 200 – 300 kg, with the large type specimen of T. garbanii estimated at 4 – 4.5 m long.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus possessed a long, low snout that terminated in a toothless beak.
facts.quote: The skull had a long, low snout that ended in a toothless beak.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had long, rod-like bones above its eyes known as palpebrals, which formed heavy bony eyebrows.
facts.quote: Long rod-like bones called palpebrals were present above the eyes, giving the animal heavy bony eyebrows.

facts.statement: Ridges on the skull and the internal position of the teeth are interpreted as evidence that Thescelosaurus had muscular cheeks.
facts.quote: The ridges and position of the teeth, deeply internal to the outside surface of the skull, have been interpreted as evidence for muscular cheeks.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had six teeth in each premaxilla, a primitive trait shared only with earlier ornithischians like Lesothosaurus and Scutellosaurus.
facts.quote: The premaxillae had six teeth each, a primitive trait among ornithischians that is otherwise only found in much earlier and more basal forms such as Lesothosaurus and Scutellosaurus.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had a very long tail that constituted half of its total body length.
facts.quote: The tail was long and made up half of the total body length.

facts.statement: Large, thin, flat mineralized plates known as intercostal plates were found along the sides of the ribs in Thescelosaurus.
facts.quote: Large thin and flat mineralized plates have been found next to the ribs' sides, so-called intercostal plates.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus is distinguished from closely related genera by having a femur that is longer than its tibia.
facts.quote: The femur (thigh bone) was longer than the tibia (shin bone), which distinguishes the genus from closely related genera.

facts.statement: Only the first three fingers of Thescelosaurus ended in hoof-like claws.
facts.quote: Only the first three digits ended in hooflike unguals.

facts.statement: Most of Thescelosaurus's weight was supported by the center three toes, with the middle toe being the longest.
facts.quote: Most of the animal's weight was therefore supported by the center three digits, of which the middle (third) was the longest.

facts.statement: Skin impressions from a 2022-discovered Tanis specimen show that parts of Thescelosaurus were covered in scales.
facts.quote: In 2022, news media reported that the Tanis specimen preserves skin impressions on a leg that show that parts of the animal were covered in scales.

facts.statement: In 2008, Galton argued that scutes previously interpreted as belonging to Thescelosaurus were actually of crocodilian origin.
facts.quote: Galton argued in 2008 that Morris's scutes are crocodilian in origin.

facts.statement: Charles Gilmore initially classified Thescelosaurus as a member of the family Camptosauridae in 1913.
facts.quote: In his 1913 description of Thescelosaurus, Gilmore considered it to be a member of Camptosauridae, alongside Hypsilophodon, Dryosaurus and Laosaurus.

facts.statement: Charles Gilmore reclassified Thescelosaurus into the family Hypsilophodontidae in 1915.
facts.quote: In 1915, he instead placed it within Hypsilophodontidae alongside only Hypsilophodon.

facts.statement: Galton assigned Thescelosaurus to Iguanodontidae in 1974 based on leg proportions but reverted to Hypsilophodontidae in 1995 after finding Iguanodontidae to be an unnatural group.
facts.quote: Galton classified Thescelosaurus as a member of Iguanodontidae based on hindlimb proportions in 1974, but this family was found to be polyphyletic (not a natural group); he therefore returned to a hypsilophodontid classification in 1995.

facts.statement: Boyd and colleagues identified a clade of early ornithopods including Thescelosaurus, Parksosaurus, Zephyrosaurus, Orodromeus, and Oryctodromeus.
facts.quote: Boyd and colleagues found support for a larger group of early ornithopods consisting of Thescelosaurus, Parksosaurus, Zephyrosaurus, Orodromeus and Oryctodromeus.

facts.statement: Scientists disagree on whether Thescelosaurus belongs to the Ornithopoda or represents a more basal group of dinosaurs.
facts.quote: There is also disagreement about whether Thescelosaurus and thescelosaurids are members of Ornithopoda or more basal.

facts.statement: Boyd argued in 2015 that there was no definitive proof Thescelosaurus was an ornithopod because many studies lacked marginocephalians or remained unresolved.
facts.quote: Boyd highlighted in 2015 that many phylogenetic studies that included Thescelosaurus either do not include marginocephalians or are unresolved, so there was no definitive evidence that Thescelosaurus was an ornithopod.

facts.statement: Fonseca and colleagues named the clade Pyrodontia to unite Thescelosaurus with derived ornithischians when the group is placed outside Ornithopoda.
facts.quote: Fonseca and colleagues gave the name Pyrodontia to the clade uniting Thescelosaurus with more derived ornithischians when Thescelosauridae is outside Ornithopoda, referencing the early and rapid diversification of Thescelosauridae, Marginocephalia and Ornithopoda.

facts.statement: A 2024 study identified the Late Jurassic Nanosaurus as the earliest known thescelosaurid.
facts.quote: In 2024, André Fonseca and colleagues recovered the Late Jurassic Nanosaurus as the earliest thescelosaurid, which would shorten the ghost lineage.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus was likely a herbivore, similar to other ornithischian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Like other ornithischians, Thescelosaurus was probably herbivorous.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus likely fed selectively on specific plants, indicated by its varied teeth and narrow snout.
facts.quote: The different types of teeth, as well as the narrow snout, suggest that it was a selective feeder.

facts.statement: A fossil specimen of Thescelosaurus shows a bone pathology where the long bones of its right foot were fused at the top.
facts.quote: One specimen is known to have had a bone pathology, with the long bones of the right foot fused at their tops.

facts.statement: In 1915, Gilmore proposed that Thescelosaurus was an agile, two-legged animal adapted for running.
facts.quote: In his 1915 description, Gilmore suggested that Thescelosaurus was an agile, bipedal (two-legged) animal and was adapted for running.

facts.statement: In 1974, Galton suggested that Thescelosaurus might have occasionally moved on all fours due to its long arms and wide hands.
facts.quote: Galton, in 1974, even suggested that Thescelosaurus could have occasionally moved quadrupedally (on all fours), given its fairly long arms and wide hands.

facts.statement: In 2023, Senter and Mackey concluded that a quadrupedal posture was theoretically possible because the spine could bend down to let the hands touch the ground.
facts.quote: Phil Senter and Jared Mackey, in 2023, concluded that a quadrupedal posture would have been theoretically possible, as the spine of the back was bent down, allowing the hand to touch the ground even when the hind limbs were straight.

facts.statement: Senter and Mackey noted that in a quadrupedal posture the fingers would point sideways, making forward propulsion unlikely and suggesting quadrupedal locomotion is improbable.
facts.quote: However, in such a posture the fingers would have pointed towards the sides rather than front, and consequently could not have been used to propel the animal forward; quadrupedal locomotion therefore seems unlikely.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had an enlarged anterior semicircular canal in its inner ear, suggesting acute balance sensitivity that could indicate high agility or burrowing behavior.
facts.quote: The second trait is found in the inner ear, which contains the three semicircular canals that house the sense of balance: one of these canals, the anterior semicircular canal, was greatly enlarged, suggesting acute balance sensitivity, which in turn might suggest high agility but could also be explained by possible burrowing behavior.

facts.statement: Button and Zanno argued that Thescelosaurus held its head slightly up-tilted when the lateral semicircular canal was horizontal.
facts.quote: Button and Zanno argued that the head of Thescelosaurus would be slightly up-tilted when oriented such that the canal is horizontal.

facts.statement: The hypothesis that Thescelosaurus rib plates were armor for defense was refuted because Sharpey's fibers indicate they were embedded in muscle rather than being osteoderms.
facts.quote: It was originally suggested that they were osteoderms (armor) for defence against predators. This hypothesis has been refuted, as both their outer and inner surfaces show Sharpey's fibres, indicating the insertion of tendons – consequently, the plates must have been completely embedded within the musculature.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus rib plates may have aided breathing or increased the rigidity of the thoracic cavity.
facts.quote: Instead, the plates may have played a role in breathing, or simply made the thoracic cavity more rigid.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus rib plates were absent in smaller specimens, suggesting they ossified only later in life.
facts.quote: The plates appear to be absent in smaller Thescelosaurus specimens, suggesting that they ossified only later in life.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had a small brain similar in size to ceratopsids like Triceratops, suggesting cognitive abilities within the range of modern reptiles.
facts.quote: Overall, the brain was small compared to most other neornithischian dinosaurs, but similar in size to that of ceratopsids such as Triceratops. Its cognitive abilities were therefore likely within the range of modern reptiles.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had an acute sense of smell, with olfactory bulbs making up around 3% of the brain endocast volume.
facts.quote: The sense of smell, in contrast, was acute, as indicated by the large olfactory bulbs of the brain, which are around 3% of the entire volume of the endocast.

facts.statement: Button and Zanno suggested Thescelosaurus may have been semi-fossorial due to its poor hearing and acute sense of smell, traits common in burrowing animals.
facts.quote: Poor hearing and an acute sense of smell are commonly found in modern animals that create burrows, leading Button and Zanno to suggest that Thescelosaurus may have been semi-fossorial.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus might have dug for food like roots and tubers, which it could detect with its acute sense of smell.
facts.quote: The animal might have dug for food such as roots and tubers, which can be detected by smelling.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had robust forelimbs and fused premaxillae that reinforced the snout tip, features that could aid in digging.
facts.quote: Some anatomical features of the skeleton could also be related to digging, such as the robust forelimbs and the premaxillae that were fused together towards their tips, reinforcing the tip of the snout to aid in digging.

facts.statement: Button and Zanno alternatively suggested that Thescelosaurus may have inherited burrowing adaptations from ancestors without actually burrowing itself.
facts.quote: Button and Zanno alternatively suggested that Thescelosaurus could have inherited its burrowing adaptations from burrowing ancestors, while not burrowing itself.

facts.statement: In 2000, researchers interpreted a chest concretion in the "Willo" specimen as a fossilized heart with three low-density areas resembling ventricles and an aorta.
facts.quote: In 2000, the imaging specialist Paul Fisher and colleagues interpreted a concretion in the chest region of the "Willo" specimen as the remnant of a heart.

facts.statement: In 2001, Timothy Rowe and colleagues argued that the object was not a heart because it engulfed a rib and had concentric internal layers.
facts.quote: In 2001, Timothy Rowe and colleagues commented that the anatomy of the object is inconsistent with a heart – for example, the supposed heart partially engulfs one of the ribs and has an internal structure of concentric layers in some places.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus lived in western North America during the late Maastrichtian age, approximately 66.04 million years ago, just before the extinction event.
facts.quote: Thescelosaurus is definitively known only from deposits in western North America dating to the late Maastrichtian age, just before the Cretaceous-Paleogene Extinction Event 66.04 million years ago.

facts.statement: Different species of Thescelosaurus are found in the Lance Formation of Wyoming, the Hell Creek Formation of South Dakota and Montana, and the Frenchman Formation of Saskatchewan.
facts.quote: T. neglectus is known from the Lance Formation of Wyoming and the Hell Creek Formation of South Dakota, T. garbanii is known from the Hell Creek Formation of Montana, and T. assiniboiensis is known from the Frenchman Formation of Saskatchewan.

facts.statement: A 2011 unbiased census study estimated that Thescelosaurus made up 8% of the dinosaur fauna in the Hell Creek Formation.
facts.quote: A 2011 census study of an area of the Hell Creek Formation where fossils have been collected without such bias estimated that Thescelosaurus forms 8% of the dinosaur fauna.

facts.statement: In 2011, researchers estimated Thescelosaurus was the most abundant dinosaur in the Frenchman Formation, representing 31% of specimens.
facts.quote: Brown and colleagues, in 2011, estimated that Thescelosaurus was perhaps the most abundant dinosaur in the Frenchman Formation, accounting for 31% of specimens.

facts.statement: At a specific locality in the Frenchman Formation, Thescelosaurus fossils accounted for 42% of all tetrapod fossils, and all were small, likely juvenile individuals.
facts.quote: At the 'convenience store' locality of the Frenchman Formation, Thescelosaurus even accounted for 42% of all tetrapod fossils; all Thescelosaurus specimens from this locality are very small and presumably juvenile.

facts.statement: Foot phalanges are the most common identifiable Thescelosaurus fossils, while complete articulated skeletons are very rare.
facts.quote: The most common Thescelosaurus fossils that can be readily identified are the phalanges of the foot, while articulated skeletons are very rare.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately between 72 and 66 million years ago, from the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico, aproximadamente entre 72 y 66 millones de años, desde el Campaniense al Maastrichtiense

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus was one of the last members of the fauna before the Cretaceous-Tertiary extinction event around 65.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fue uno de los últimos miembros de la fauna antes del evento de extinción del Cretacio-Terciario alrededor de 65.5 millones de años atrás

facts.statement: Fossils of Thescelosaurus have been found in formations representing the western shore of the Western Interior Seaway that divided western and eastern North America during the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The formations where Thescelosaurus fossils have been found represent different sections of the western shore of the Western Interior Seaway dividing western and eastern North America during the Cretaceous

facts.statement: The paleoenvironment of Thescelosaurus was likely a swampy to lowland forest with a conifer canopy and a diverse angiosperm-dominated mid-canopy and understory.
facts.quote: The paleoenvironment would have been a swampy to lowland forest with a tree canopy of conifers and a diverse angiosperm-dominated mid-canopy and understory

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the disproportional presence of Thescelosaurus fossils in sandstone compared to ceratopsians in mudstone might indicate a preference for habitats along channel margins rather than floodplains.
facts.quote: The disproportional presence of Thescelosaurus and hadrosaurs in sandstone, versus ceratopsians in mudstone, could suggest that Thescelosaurus preferred the habitat along channel margins rather than floodplains

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus inhabited an ecomorphospace distinct from other dinosaurs, including similarly sized and built pachycephalosaurids.
facts.quote: Thescelosaurus would have inhabited an ecomorphospace different from that of other dinosaurs including the similarly sized and built pachycephalosaurids

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus was a bipedal ornithopod known from partial skeletons and skulls indicating a length of around 2.5 to 4 meters.
facts.quote: Este ornitópodo bípedo se conoce por varios esqueletos parciales y los cráneos que indican que medían alrededor de 2,5 a 4 metros de largo

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus had robust hind limbs, small and wide hands, and a head with a very elongated snout.
facts.quote: Tenía los miembros traseros robustos, las manos pequeñas y anchas, y una cabeza con un hocico muy alargado

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus is considered a specialized basal ornithopod and a hypsilophodontid herbivore.
facts.quote: Este género de dinosaurio es considerado como un ornitópodo basal especializado, un hipsilofodóntido herbívoro

facts.statement: The genus attracted media attention in 2000 when a specimen unearthed in 1993 in South Dakota was interpreted as including a fossilized heart.
facts.quote: El género atrajo la atención de los medios en 2000, cuando un espécimen desenterrado en 1993 en Dakota del Sur fue interpretado como incluyendo a un corazón fósil

facts.statement: There was much debate over whether the remains were truly from such an organ, and many scientists now doubt the identification of the object and its implications.
facts.quote: Hubo mucha discusión sobre si los restos eran realmente de dicho órgano. Muchos científicos ahora dudan la identificación del objeto y las implicaciones de tal identificación

facts.statement: The genus Thescelosaurus was named by Gilmore in 1913.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Gilmore, 1913

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Thescelosaurus is Thescelosaurus neglectus.
facts.quote: type_species: Thescelosaurus neglectus

facts.statement: Four species are currently recognized as valid: Thescelosaurus neglectus, Thescelosaurus edmontonensis, Thescelosaurus garbanii, and Thescelosaurus assiniboiensis.
facts.quote: subdivision: Thescelosaurus edmontonensis Sternberg, 1940 Thescelosaurus garbanii Morris, 1976 Thescelosaurus assiniboiensis Brown, Boyd & Russell, 2011

facts.statement: Bugenasaura is a synonym of the genus Thescelosaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: Bugenasaura Galton, 1995

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus measured between 2.5 and 4 meters in length and weighed between 200 and 300 kilograms based on various specimens.
facts.quote: El tamaño del animal se ha estimado entre los 2,5 a 4.metros de largo, a partir de varios especímenes, y un peso de entre 200 a 300 kilogramos

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus was a robust biped with strong hind legs, small broad hands, a long pointed snout, and likely small armored plates along its spine.
facts.quote: Thescelosaurus era un animal bípedo de constitución fuerte. Poseía patas traseras robustas, pequeñas y amplias "manos", un morro alargado y puntiagudo, y probablemente pequeñas placas armados a lo largo de la columna.

facts.statement: Its sharp beak and front teeth suggest it could have consumed some animal material.
facts.quote: Su pico puntiagudo y sus dientes frontales le hubieran permitido ingerir alguna material animal.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus was likely a herbivore but could also have been omnivorous.
facts.quote: Thescelosaurus fue un robusto bípedo, probablemente herbívoro, pero también podría ser omnívoro.

facts.statement: It likely fed on vegetation within the first five meters of the ground, storing food in muscular cheeks before chewing.
facts.quote: Debió alimentarse en los primeros cinco metros desde el suelo, seleccionado el alimento, y almacenándolos en sus mejillas para poder luego masticarlos.

facts.statement: A prominent bone border along the entire upper jaw and lower jaw supported muscular cheeks.
facts.quote: Tenía un prominente borde a lo largo de todo su maxilar El soporte óseo para las mejillas, y un borde en ambos dentarios, el hueso con dientes en la mandíbula inferior.

facts.statement: Its skull featured primitive upper beak teeth and long bony bars over the eyes that formed heavy eyebrow ridges.
facts.quote: El cráneo también tenía dientes en el premaxilar, o pico superior, un rasgo primitivo entre ornitópodos, y huesos similares a barras largos llamados palpebrales sobre los ojos, dándole unas pesadas cejas huesudas.

facts.statement: Its teeth consisted of two types: small pointed front teeth and leaf-shaped cheek teeth.
facts.quote: Los dientes eran de dos dos tipos, pequeños dientes puntiagudos al frente y dientes con forma de hojas en las mejillas.

facts.statement: It had short, broad five-fingered hands, walked on the tips of four toes ending in hoof-like casings, and possessed a long tail stiffened by ossified tendons.
facts.quote: Tenía las manos cortas, amplias, con cinco dedos, pisaba con la punta de los cuatro dedos de cada pie terminados en una especie de casco formada por la última falange de cada dedo y una cola larga sostenida por la osificación de los tendones desde la sección media hasta al final de la misma, que habría reducido la flexibilidad de esta.

facts.statement: Fine bone plates were found along its sides and ribs, though their function remains unknown.
facts.quote: Se han encontrado finas placas de hueso junto a sus costados y costillas, siendo su función desconocida hasta el momento.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Thescelosaurus could have moved on all fours due to its long arms and broad hands, though this hypothesis is not supported in scientific literature.
facts.quote: Este animal pudo haberse movido sobre sus cuatro miembros, dados que sus brazos eran lo bastante largos y sus manos anchas, pero esta idea no se ha tenido en cuenta en la literatura científica, aunque aparece en trabajos de divulgación.

facts.statement: One specimen showed a bone pathology where the right metatarsus fused with others, hindering rapid movement.
facts.quote: Un espécimen presenta una patología ósea, en el metatarso del pie derecho y se fundió en los otros, obstaculizando el movimiento rápido.

facts.statement: The function of the rib-side plates is unknown; while they might have aided respiration, the lack of muscle attachment scars argues against this role.
facts.quote: Su función es desconocida, pudiendo haber desempeñado un papel en la respiración. Sin embargo, no se han encontrado en las placas una cicatriz o marca como indicación de la inserción muscular, lo que apunta contra una función respiratoria.

facts.statement: Recent histological studies suggest these plates may have started as cartilage and ossified as the animal aged.
facts.quote: Un estudio histológico reciente de las placas acodadas de un probable subadulto indica que pudieron haber comenzado como cartílago y se convirtieron en hueso mientras que el animal envejecía.

facts.statement: A 2022 documentary reported that a Thescelosaurus specimen supposedly died on the day of the K-Pg extinction, covered in skin impressions including long scales on its legs.
facts.quote: En su documental de 2022, Dinosaurs: The Final Day , Sir David Attenborough informó que un espécimen de Thescelosaurus supuestamente murió el día de la extinción de K-Pg , cubierto de impresiones en la piel que incluían escamas alargadas sobre las piernas.

facts.statement: Charles M. Sternberg reconstructed the arm orientation as nearly perpendicular to the body, while another theory suggests it extended along the flank.
facts.quote: Charles M. Sternberg los reconstruyó con el brazo orientado casi perpendicular al cuerpo, otra idea es que se extendía por el flanco.

facts.statement: Peter Galton noted that most ornithischians, including Thescelosaurus, had humeri articulating with the shoulder via the entire bone end rather than a spherical joint like mammals.
facts.quote: Como apuntó Peter Galton, el húmero de la mayoría de los ornitisquios articulaba con el hombro por una superficie articular que consistía en el extremo entero del hueso, en vez de una articulación esférica como en los mamíferos.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus was likely slower than other hypsilophodontids due to its heavier build and leg structure.
facts.quote: Thescelosaurus era probablemente más lento que otros "hipsilofodóntidos", debido a su estructura más pesada y de la estructura de la pierna.

facts.statement: Unlike Hypsilophodon and other running animals, Thescelosaurus had unusual hind limbs where the thigh bone was longer than the shin bone.
facts.quote: Comparado con ellos, tenía miembros traseros inusuales, porque en la pierna era más larga que la espinilla, al contrario que en Hypsilophodon y animales corredores en general.

facts.statement: Because shields were not found in other articulated specimens, it is debated whether Morris's suggested shields were actually crocodilian in origin.
facts.quote: Los escudos no se ha encontrado con otros especímenes articulados de Thescelosaurus, sugiriendo que los escudos de Morris podrían ser de origen cocodriliano.

facts.statement: Paul Barrett noted that the skin impressions indicate Thescelosaurus was not feathered, unlike other small neornithischians.
facts.quote: En una entrevista de seguimiento, Paul Barrett ha señalado que esto significa que Thescelosaurus no estaba emplumado como se suponía para otros pequeños neornitisquios.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen USNM 7757 was discovered in 1891 by paleontologists John Bell Hatcher and William H. Utterback.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Thescelosaurus, USNM 7757, fue descubierto en 1891 por los paleontólogos John Bell Hatcher y William H. Utterback

facts.statement: It lived during the Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian in the Lance Formation of Niobrara and Converse counties, Wyoming, USA.
facts.quote: fue descubierto en 1891 por los paleontólogos John Bell Hatcher y William H. Utterback, provenientes de los sedimentos del Maastrichtiense durante el Cretácico Superior de la Formación Lance en los condados de Niobrara y Converse, Wyoming, Estados Unidos

facts.statement: Charles W. Gilmore prepared the skeleton for description in a 1913 paper, naming it T. neglectus.
facts.quote: Charles W. Gilmore del Museo Nacional de Historia Natural de la Institución Smithsoniana los preparó para su descripción en un corto trabajo en 1913, llamándolos T. neglectus

facts.statement: The skeleton remained in its shipping boxes for years before being prepared by Charles W. Gilmore.
facts.quote: El esqueleto, sin embargo, permaneció en sus cajas de envío por años hasta que Charles W. Gilmore del Museo Nacional de Historia Natural de la Institución Smithsoniana los preparó para su descripción en un corto trabajo en 1913

facts.statement: The type specimen was found mostly in a natural, articulated position, missing only the head and neck due to erosion.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo fue encontrado en gran parte en una posición natural y articulado faltando solamente la cabeza y el cuello, debido a la erosión

facts.statement: The name comes from Gilmore's surprise at finding such a good specimen that had been neglected for so long.
facts.quote: El nombre viene de la sorpresa de Gilmore en el sentido de encontrar tan buen espécimen que había sido desatendido durante tanto tiempo

facts.statement: Gilmore considered it an agile and fast creature and assigned it to Hypsilophodontidae, a family of small bipedal dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Lo consideraba como una criatura ágil y rápida, y lo asignó a Hypsilophodontidae, una familia de pequeños dinosaurios bípedos

facts.statement: A well-preserved but slightly older skeleton from the Horseshoe Canyon Formation of Alberta, Canada, was named T. warreni by William Parks in 1926.
facts.quote: Otro esqueleto bien preservado pero levemente más viejo de la Formación Horseshoe Canyon, de Alberta, Canadá, fue nombrado T. warreni por William Parks en 1926

facts.statement: Charles M. Sternberg assigned it its own genus, Parksosaurus, in 1937 due to large differences with T. neglectus.
facts.quote: Este esqueleto presenta grandes diferencias con T. neglectus, y llevó a Charles M. Sternberg a asignarle su propio género, Parksosaurus, en 1937

facts.statement: Since Peter Galton's 1974 review, T. edmontonensis has been considered a more robust specimen, possibly of another sex of the T. neglectus type.
facts.quote: T. edmontonensis desde la revisión de Peter Galton en 1974 ha sido considerado un ejemplar más robusto, posiblemente de otro sexo del espécimen tipo de T. neglectus

facts.statement: However, Boyd and colleagues found it could not be assigned to a valid Thescelosaurus species, and the specimen is still viewed as incertae sedis in the genus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Boyd y colegas encontraron que no podría asignarlo tampoco a la especie válida de Thescelosaurus y el espécimen es visto hasta la fecha como un incertae sedis en el género

facts.statement: A point of discussion regarding T. edmontonensis is the ankle, which Galton believed was damaged and misinterpreted, but which William J. Morris saw in 1976 as truly different from T. neglectus.
facts.quote: otro punto de discusión con respecto a T. edmontonensis es el tobillo, que Galton creyó que estaba dañado y malinterpretado, pero que fue visto por William J. Morris en 1976 como verdaderamente diferente de T. neglectus

facts.statement: Morris described specimen SDSM 7210 as an unidentified Thescelosaurus species consisting of a partial skull with heavy jaw and cheek ridges, two partial vertebrae, and two finger bones.
facts.quote: Morris describió un espécimen, SDSM 7210, que consiste en un cráneo parcial con los cantos pesados en la quijada inferior y la mejilla, dos vértebras parciales, y dos huesos de los dedos como una especie no identificada de Thescelosaurus

facts.statement: Morris paid attention to deeply inserted premaxillary tooth rows, interpreting them as support for the presence of muscular cheeks.
facts.quote: Prestó mucha atención a línea de dientes premaxilares profundamente insertados que interpretó como apoyo para la presencia de mejillas musculares

facts.statement: This skull was recognized as an unnamed hypsilophodontid for many years until Galton erected it as the type specimen of the new genus and species Bugenasaura infernalis.
facts.quote: Este cráneo fue reconocido como un hipsilofodóntido sin nombre durante muchos años, hasta que Galton lo erigiera como espécimen tipo de un nuevo género y especie Bugenasaura infernalis

facts.statement: Morris named a new possible Thescelosaurus species for specimen LACM 33542 as T. garbanii?, with a question mark because it was uncertain whether it belonged to the genus.
facts.quote: Morris nombró a una nueva posible especie de Thescelosaurus para el espécimen, LACM 33542, como T. garbanii?, con un signo de interrogación porque era incierto que perteneciera al género

facts.statement: LACM 33542 consisted of a partial hind limb, one-third larger than those described for T. neglectus and Parksosaurus, or nearly twice as large as that of Hypsilophodon.
facts.quote: LACM 33542 estaba constituido de un miembro trasero parcial, un tercio más grande que los descritos para T. neglectus y Parksosaurus o casi dos veces más grande que el de Hypsilophodon

facts.statement: The specimen was discovered by amateur paleontologist Harley Garbani, from whom it derives its name.
facts.quote: El espécimen fue descubierto por el paleontólogo aficionado Harley Garbani de donde proviene su nombre

facts.statement: T. garbanii may have measured nearly 4.5 meters in length, being larger than the largest T. neglectus.
facts.quote: T. garbanii pudo haber medido cerca de 4,5 metros de largo, siendo más grande que el mayor de los T. neglectus

facts.statement: However, scientific literature has favored Galton's opinion that T. edmontonensis is not different from T. neglectus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la literatura científica ha favorecido la opinión de Galton sobre eso, T. edmontonensis no es diferente de T. neglectus

facts.statement: In the same Bugenasaura description work, Galton demonstrated that the way Morris connected T. garbanii and T. edmontonensis was the result of subsequent ankle damage.
facts.quote: En el mismo trabajo de descripción de Bugenasaura, Galton demostró que la manera en que Morris había conectado a T. garbanii y T. edmontonensis fue el resultado del daño en el tobillo ocurrido posteriormente

facts.statement: To better accommodate this species, Galton suggested it belonged to his new genus Bugenasaura as B. garbanii, though he also observed it could belong to the same-sized pachycephalosaur Stygimoloch, or be part of a third unknown dinosaur.
facts.quote: Para acomodar mejor esta especie, Galton sugirió que perteneció a su nuevo género Bugenasaura como B. garbanii, aunque también observara que podría pertenecer al paquicefalosáurido del mismo tamaño Stygimoloch, o bien ser parte de un tercer y desconocido dinosaurio

facts.statement: The group consisting of Parksosaurus and Thescelosaurus corresponds informally to Thescelosaurinae.
facts.quote: El grupo consistente en Parksosaurus y Thescelosaurus se corresponde informalmente con Thescelosaurinae

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus likely browsed low to the ground, feeding selectively while holding food in its cheeks while chewing.
facts.quote: Thescelosaurus habría ramoneado en el primer metro más o menos desde el suelo, alimentándose selectivamente, con comida sostenida en la boca por las mejillas mientras masticaba.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus was probably slower than other hypsilophodonts due to its heavier build and leg structure.
facts.quote: Thescelosaurus probablemente era más lento que otros hipsilofodontes, debido a su constitución más pesada y estructura de piernas.

facts.statement: Unlike Hypsilophodon and other running animals, Thescelosaurus had unusual hind limbs where the upper leg was longer than the shin.
facts.quote: Comparado con ellos, tenía miembros posteriores inusuales, porque la parte superior de la pierna era más larga que la espinilla , lo opuesto a Hypsilophodon y los animales que corren en general.

facts.statement: One specimen of Thescelosaurus had fused long bones in the right foot, a pathology that likely hindered rapid movement.
facts.quote: Se sabe que un espécimen tenía una patología ósea, con los huesos largos del pie derecho fusionados en la parte superior, lo que dificultaba el movimiento rápido.

facts.statement: Dental examinations and comparisons with the contemporary pachycephalosaur Stegoceras suggest Thescelosaurus was a selective feeder, allowing it to coexist without competing for food.
facts.quote: Los exámenes de los dientes de Thescelosaurus y las comparaciones con el paquicefalosáurido contemporáneo Stegoceras sugieren que Thescelosaurus era un alimentador selectivo, mientras que Stegoceras era un alimentador más indiscriminado, lo que permitía que ambos animales compartieran el mismo entorno sin competir por la comida.

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus belongs to the parent group Thescelosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Thescelosaurinae

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus is classified in the family Thescelosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Thescelosauridae

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus is a member of the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Thescelosaurus lived from the Turonian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 93.9 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Maastrichtian (93.9 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 55 recorded fossil occurrences of Thescelosaurus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 55
